current_date: Adopted under delegated powers 12 March 2025 (published March 2025; replaces March 2023 list; review due 2027)
current_evidence: The council's 'How to apply for planning permission' page links 'Planning Application Validation Requirements 2025.pdf' (this URL) and calls it the latest PAVR adopted March 2025; the only consultation page found is the closed 2022 one, and search found no newer version.

issues.detail: Householder is recorded as '(none) - national requirements only', but the PAVR has a Householder section with local requirements: site photos (side/rear extensions or alterations); parking plan (where bedrooms are added or parking/driveways are affected); arboricultural survey (where protected or significant trees are affected); heritage impact assessment (where a listed building, its curtilage or setting is affected); window and door drawings/details (where windows/doors change in an Article 4 area); plus information asked for in pre-application advice.
issues.evidence: Section 2 Householder applications, para 2.3 'likely to be required'

issues.detail: Reserved matters, Listed building consent, Lawful development cert, Demolition in cons area, Variation of condition s73, Discharge of conditions, NMA, Works to trees, PiP and S106 modification are all '(none)', but each has its own PAVR section with local requirements. Examples: LBC needs a schedule of works and methodology plus a heritage impact assessment (where significance is notably affected); LDC s191 needs statutory declarations and a hatched site plan (where multiple uses are claimed); s73 needs a marketing report (removing occupancy/restrictive use conditions), an updated ecological appraisal (host survey >2 years old) and an updated AIA (>5 years old); RM needs daylight/sunlight (where scale is considered with significant shading) and BIAM (5+ dwellings or 1,000 sqm); TPO works need an AIA for removals and evidence of structural damage where that is the basis; approval of details needs the Annex D conditions schedule. Grokbot even captured the 'Conditions proforma' text in tab_items but still marked Discharge of conditions '(none)'.

Full planning local requirements in para 4.3 that Grokbot missed: conveyancing plan (public/private spaces), topographical survey (major), phasing plan (phased major), drawing schedule (major), housing accommodation schedule (major residential, Annex E template), housing statement (major residential outside settlement boundaries or >31% affordable), health impact assessment (50+ dwellings or any C2), site waste management plan (major or significant demolition), digital connectivity statement (all new premises), planning obligations statement (major), and retail impact on the Primary Shopping Area (>900 sqm in CMK).

Most Full planning trigger excerpts are Annex B definition fragments, policy text or the wrong item's text, not when the requirement applies. 'Archaeological Assessment' shows the BIAM definition; 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage' shows the soil quality / sports and open space text; 'Tall buildings / Wind microclimate' shows the Design and access statement definition; 'Environmental Statement' shows a rule about paper copies for parish councils; 'Planning Statement' shows para 15.42 boilerplate; 'Fire Statement' is cut to 'in height, a fire statement15.'; 'Flood Risk Assessment' is cut to 'or 3, a flood risk assessment; the appropriate fee.'; 'Energy / Sustainability Statement' quotes the Plan:MK 19% carbon policy. The real thresholds are missing: FRA (flood zone 2/3, or >1 ha in zone 1), energy and climate statement (11+ dwellings or 1,000 sqm), retail impact (>900 sqm gross city centre / 350 sqm elsewhere), DAS (major, 1+ dwellings, or 100 sqm+ in a conservation area), and Annex C transport thresholds.
issues.evidence: Para 4.3 triggers vs Annex B descriptions; e.g. 'Energy and climate statement: for development of 11 or more dwellings or 1,000 square metres or more of floorspace'

issues.detail: All 46 Full planning rows carry 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', and many come from other application sections. Examples: 'Habitats Regulations Assessment / SPA mitigation' is the hedgerow-removal land-type list (s14); 'Planning Obligations / S106' is the Relevant Demolition Consent exceptions list (s10); 'Heritage Statement' is the HIA for demolition in a conservation area; 'Open space / play space' and 'Telecommunications' come from the prior approval section (s15); 'Lawful development evidence (statutory declarations)' is LDC s191; 'Schedule of works' is LBC; 'Arboricultural' is works to trees in a CA. 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' under Change of use - prior approval is really the marketing report for removing occupancy conditions (s73). 'Pre-application advice' under Outline only matched the verb 'outline'; it applies to all types.

All 12 tab_items are submission process, file-format or boilerplate fragments rather than requirements: the admin fee for email/paper forms; PDF file types, file naming and the 10MB size limit; the 'Site Layout - 9453_07 Rev A.pdf).' fragment; privacy/redaction text; the 20-working-day return rule; the optional linear scale bar; and an annotated example drawing caption ('Existing photograph annotated W1 W2 W3...'). Only 'Drawing schedule' and 'Conditions proforma' are real items.

Several requirement rows reuse the same excerpt: 'Employment / Economic Statement' and 'Marketing / vacancy evidence' have identical text; 'Floor plans / Elevations' and 'Roof plan' share the householder drawing list; 'Design and Access Statement' and 'Fire Statement' come from one fragment.
List date is given as 2025-03-01, but the document says it was adopted on 12 March 2025 (the web page says 13 March 2025).

summary: The link is the current March 2025 PAVR and it works, but extraction is poor: Householder and ten other application types show '(none)' despite dedicated sections with local requirements, most Full planning triggers are definition fragments or misattributed text, and the tab_items are process boilerplate.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
